notes: Hand-authored mapping from the vendored packs (sources.json / pack.json) onto the assembler-v2 basis registry: which style lane a model belongs to, which head family / body archetype it stands in for, how it mounts onto the rig, and how each of its glTF material slots maps onto the 11 palette regions. build-lanes.mjs validates every reference against the committed pack.json manifests and emits assets/packs/lanes.json (read by scripts/pack_library.gd) plus the frontend's generated catalog, so the engine, the UI and this file can never drift.

mounts.avatar: The GLB/VRM IS the avatar: the whole procedural rig is hidden and the mesh replaces it. Registered on the HEAD basis so exactly one mesh_basis_required signal fires per rebuild.
mounts.body: Mesh body + PROCEDURAL head: the loaded rig replaces the procedural body, and the procedural head (with its ears/horns/muzzle) is re-parented onto the rig's head bone from code via BoneAttachment3D. Registered on the BODY basis.
mounts.procedural: No mesh at all — the parametric assembler builds everything. The default, and the primary for the kemono lane.

quaternius-base-v1.reason: Untextured flat-colour material slots — legal-inventory.md's 'maps perfectly onto our 7-region semantic recolor system'. Every slot is named and gets a region.

quaternius-outfits-v1.reason: Flat-colour modular garments. Split across the jrpg-bases.md 60/30/10 blocking: the peasant set is the 60 (fur), the ranger set the 30 (accent), and the bare 'Regular' body material is the 15-25% skin.

quaternius-monsters-v1.reason: Flat-colour slots, one primitive per material, so every region recolours independently. *_Main is the base coat, *_Secondary the accent — except on the three chibi kemono bipeds (cat/bunny/frog) where the secondary IS the lighter belly/muzzle countershade kemono.md describes, so it maps to innerMuzzle.

unverifiedSlots.Material.011: Unnamed Blender default on the Bunny — assigned to 'detail' by elimination, not by looking at the model. No visual audit was possible in this environment.
unverifiedSlots.Material.024: Same: unnamed Blender default on the Bunny.

quaternius-animals-v1.reason: Head/tail DONOR pack (quadruped rigs). Mapped for completeness and for the fox/wolf head-graft follow-up; no lane registers these as a basis today (see blocked[] below).

unverifiedSlots.Material: The Husky ships five unnamed Blender-default materials. Assigned by slot order (base coat, light, accent, detail, dark) WITHOUT a visual check — flagged rather than presented as verified.

vroid-cc0-v1.reason: VRoid names every material with a role suffix (_SKIN/_FACE/_EYE/_HAIR/_CLOTH), so the mapping is exact rather than heuristic. Used when the house toon shader replaces MToon on the web path (technique.md: MToon on WebGL2 is unverified upstream).

godette-v1.reason: Four named materials on a 3.4k-tri anime mascot — the cheapest anime avatar we ship and the one that fits the Quest-3 budget with room to spare.

kaykit-adventurers-v1.reason: SINGLE 1024x1024 gradient atlas per character (legal-inventory.md: 'recolor requires atlas palette-swap, not material slots'). Swapping the atlas material for a flat house material would collapse the whole character to one colour, so the vendor material is KEPT and per-region recolour is unavailable for this pack. The fix is the atlas palette-swap shader — technique.md's option A conversion is a re-UV job and Blender is not available here.

kaykit-skeletons-v1.reason: Same single-atlas texturing as the Adventurers pack, plus an emissive 'Glow' slot for the eye sockets.

polygonalmind-100avatars-v1.reason: Each avatar bakes to one atlas material (mat_NNN); the same atlas problem as KayKit. Scoped to the VRM importer corpus anyway, not to player avatars.

khronos-fox-v1.reason: One textured material on a 576-tri quadruped; it is the runtime-loader reference asset, not a player avatar.

unlaned.quaternius-animals-v1: Vendored as HEAD/TAIL DONOR geometry for the kemono graft, which the blocked[] entry below proves is not possible at runtime: every quadruped is one skinned mesh with no separable head node. They are quadrupeds, not avatars, so they are deliberately not offered as playable characters either. Kept because they remain the donor set the moment a Blender-equipped pipeline exists.
unlaned.khronos-fox-v1: The canonical quadruped skinning/animation reference asset for the runtime GLB loader tests (576 tris, mixed CC0 mesh / CC-BY-4.0 rig). A test fixture, never a player avatar.

blocked.wanted: Graft a CC0 Quaternius animal head (Fox/Wolf/Husky/Shiba) onto the Universal Base Characters humanoid rig via BoneAttachment3D, per legal-inventory.md's hybrid recommendation.
blocked.verdict: NOT POSSIBLE AT RUNTIME — measured, not assumed.
blocked.evidence: Every quadruped in quaternius-animals-v1 is ONE skinned mesh with no separable head node: wolf.glb contains exactly one mesh ('Wolf', 4 primitives) bound to a single 51-joint skin, and its head geometry is skin-weighted to the 'Head' joint rather than living in its own node. BoneAttachment3D attaches whole NODES, so there is nothing to attach; isolating the head means splitting the mesh by bone weight, which is offline mesh surgery.
blocked.blocker: Blender (or an equivalent weight-aware mesh splitter) is not installed in this environment, and gltf-transform has no split-by-skin-weight operation.
blocked.shippedInstead: The 'body' mount: the CC0 mesh body carries a fully PROCEDURAL beast head (kemono-ubc-body-hard/soft entries above), plus the three Ultimate Monsters chibi bipeds as complete meshes. The species silhouette rides on the procedural ears/horns/muzzle, which technique.md notes is where species identity actually lives.

blocked.wanted: Per-region recolour on the KayKit Adventurers/Skeletons and 100Avatars lines.
blocked.evidence: Each of those characters renders from ONE material backed by a single baked atlas, so binding it to a flat house material would paint the entire character one colour.
blocked.blocker: The fix is either an atlas palette-swap shader (needs the atlas cell layout, an art task) or re-UVing onto the palette strip (a Blender job).
blocked.shippedInstead: The vendor material is preserved and the UI marks these entries 'fixed colours'.
